sec: Pre-renal vs ATN exceptions & pathophysiology · p797

items.q: Match the three conditions bracketed together as 'pre-renal >> ATN' in drug/insult-induced AKI — 1) NSAIDs  2) Rhabdomyolysis  3) Polyuria (contrast-induced AKI) … A) Pre-renal component predominates over ATN
opts: All three have a pre-renal component predominant over ATN
None of them has a pre-renal component
items.exp: NSAIDs, rhabdomyolysis and polyuria (contrast-induced AKI) are bracketed together as 'pre-renal >> ATN', i.e. the pre-renal component predominates. (Book p797)

items.q: Which is the commonest form of pre-renal failure described in the pathophysiology section?
items.exp: Pathophysiology 1: non-oliguric failure (m/c). Oliguric pre-renal failure occurs only with renal vasoconstriction (NSAIDs/hypercalcemia/HRS). (Book p797)

items.q: Oliguric pre-renal failure occurs only with renal vasoconstriction, as with NSAIDs, hypercalcemia or hepatorenal syndrome.
opts: False — oliguric pre-renal failure occurs with any volume depletion
False — oliguric failure is the rule in all pre-renal AKI
items.exp: Oliguric pre-renal failure occurs only with renal vasoconstriction (NSAIDs/hypercalcemia/HRS); otherwise pre-renal failure is non-oliguric. (Book p797)

items.q: Complete the flowchart of long-standing profound pre-renal failure — 1) Resulting tubular lesion  2) Feedback mechanism  3) Consequences … A) Tubuloglomerular feedback by macula densa → ↓GFR → ↓urine output  B) Ischemic ATN
items.exp: Flowchart: long-standing profound pre-renal failure → ischemic ATN → tubuloglomerular feedback by macula densa → ↓GFR → ↓urine output. (Book p797)

items.q: Fill up: In ischemic ATN, tubuloglomerular feedback is mediated by the ______.
items.exp: Tubuloglomerular feedback by the macula densa causes ↓GFR and ↓urine output in ischemic ATN. (Book p797)

items.q: The two broad mechanisms of ATN are:
opts: Immune complex deposition and complement activation
items.exp: Renal AKI — ATN: ischemia and toxins (the toxins being endogenous and exogenous). (Book p797)

items.q: Match each endogenous toxin with its source — 1) Hemoglobin  2) Myoglobin  3) Uric acid  4) Light chains … A) Multiple myeloma  B) Hemolysis  C) Rhabdomyolysis  D) Uric acid nephropathy
items.exp: Endogenous toxins causing ATN: hemoglobin (hemolysis), myoglobin (rhabdomyolysis), uric acid (uric acid nephropathy) and light chains (multiple myeloma). (Book p797)

items.q: A patient in a crush injury develops AKI with pigmented urine. Which endogenous toxin is responsible?
items.exp: Endogenous toxin list: hemoglobin (hemolysis), myoglobin (rhabdomyolysis), uric acid (uric acid nephropathy) and light chains (multiple myeloma). (Book p797)

items.q: Fill up: In ATN, the two listed exogenous toxins are drugs and ______.
items.exp: Exogenous toxins in ATN: drugs and contrast. (Book p797)

items.q: The ATN histology figure is labelled with flattened epithelium and intraluminal debris. These changes correspond to:
opts: Tubular injury of acute tubular necrosis
Interstitial infiltrate of acute interstitial nephritis
items.exp: The ATN figure labels flattened epithelium and intraluminal debris, the histological correlates of tubular injury in ATN. (Book p797)

items.q: Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN) is caused by:
opts: Hypersensitivity reactions — drugs, infections and infiltration
Ischemic injury of the proximal tubule alone, without any immune mechanism
Contrast media alone, acting through medullary hypoxia and tubular injury
Cholesterol embolization of small renal vessels from an aortic plaque
items.exp: AIN (hypersensitivity reactions): drugs; infections — leptospirosis and scrub typhus; infiltration — lymphoma and sarcoidosis. (Book p797)

items.q: Match the AIN subgroups — 1) Infections  2) Infiltration … A) Lymphoma and sarcoidosis  B) Leptospirosis and scrub typhus
items.exp: AIN causes: drugs; infections — leptospirosis, scrub typhus; infiltration — lymphoma, sarcoidosis. (Book p797)

items.q: All but one of the following are listed causes of acute interstitial nephritis. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Leptospirosis/scrub typhus (infections) and lymphoma (infiltration) cause AIN; ethylene glycol is an ATN toxin producing oxalate urine crystals. (Book p797)

items.q: Rhabdomyolysis is listed both as a pre-renal cause (third-space sequestration) and as a cause of ATN through myoglobin.
opts: True — it appears in both lists
False — it causes only pre-renal AKI
True, but only when urine pH is alkaline
items.exp: Rhabdomyolysis appears under third-space sequestration (pre-renal) and as an endogenous ATN toxin (myoglobin), explaining why 'pre-renal >> ATN' is bracketed for it. (Book p797)
